## Before Next Class

### Submit Dig Deeper Assignment

- **compare and contrast news article to research article.**

- **include at least one detail from each section.**

- **keep it short :**

  - you don't want (or need) to write a lot

  - professor doesn't have time to read a lot :(

### Gonna Keep Reading Articles

1.  [**Sampling Error**](https://youtu.be/fp1xsBMSBg0)**.** Professor recorded a video on sampling error and sampling bias, and a stats review of null hypothesis significance testing. We will review next class....come with questions?
2.  [**Critical Questions to Evaluate Sampling Bias**](https://youtu.be/-KE3pTzYljs)**.** Professor narrates a video to help evaluate whether a sample is biased or not, and how this bias might influence the results.
3.  [**“A WEIRD View of Human Nature”**](https://www.dropbox.com/s/p9rszc3afaiwmcs/2010_WEIRDinScience.pdf?dl=0)**.** A short article that describes how most psychologists get samples for their studies. Focus on : the definition of WEIRD, how frequently psychologists conduct cross-cultural research, how different types of results in psychology differ depending on culture.
4.  [**Chapter 7, Section 36**](https://kpu.pressbooks.pub/psychmethods4e/chapter/conducting-surveys/)**.** From your textbook, on samples and populations, and different forms of sampling biases.

**Last one of the semester. Post in the VISION BOARD and only the VISION BOARD.**

1.  Focus on the article you are using for the DIG DEEPER project. Write out the main idea from the article as a linear model.

2.  Who is the population for this research question, and why are they the population?

3.  Include a screenshot (or copy or paste the text) with information about the sample described in the research article. (If there was more than one study, choose one that you are most interested in.)

4.  Does this sample seem representative of the population? Why / why not?

5.  FINALLY : include any questions you have about sampling error. I know y'all have questions...this stuff is confusing so put SOMETHING here it takes a village to learn so asking questions is part of the village I guess this metaphor is going nowhere...

6.  REPLY TO ANOTHER STUDENT : look over their response...explain how a different sample of people (or animals) studied might influence the results.
